speaker: karlhauch
text: Thank you, Councillor George. Good evening, everyone. We'll call this meeting to order. Is there any additions, deletions, or changes to the agenda, administration?

speaker: judyschuelertow
text: Nothing from us, Mr. Mayor.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Okay, is there anything from council? Okay, look for a motion then to approve or adopt the agenda as presented. Councillor Pat? I think Pat's on mute. I can't read lips.

speaker: patlee
text: I love this game. There you go. Okay, I move that we accept the agenda as presented.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Thank you very much, Councillor Pat. Anyone opposed to that motion? And the motion's carried. This evening, we're very fortunate. We have a delegation. Our inspector, Mike McCauley from Fort Saskatchewan is with us this evening to run through his detachment crime statistics. Happy New Year, Inspector Mike, and glad to have you with us, and you have the floor. Please let us know if you want questions at the end of your presentation, or during, or?

speaker: mikemccauley
text: Maybe just because it's digital, maybe at the end. So, and I'll be quick, but I have only an hour, while I've prepared 59 minutes worth of material. So, I'll open it up for questions.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Thank you.

speaker: mikemccauley
text: Thank you for having me. So, very, very briefly, I have an easy staffing update. The staffing update is that we are fully staffed, which is fantastic. As of February 11th, we will, I shouldn't, I'm currently before the horse. On February 11th, we'll be fully staffed. We have a new corporal coming from Parkland, called, her name is Corporal Jolie Marianich, good Ukrainian gal, and she's excited to join us. She lives in Sherwood Park, so she's been a corporal for a few years already, and she's laterally over. And that will complete our staff. We'll have all of our management, and we'll just be short. Two long-term sick leave members in the constable rank, which is fantastic, because I can remember three or four years ago, presenting to you folks, and we were down about 30%. So, we're in really good shape. In terms of stats, I forwarded the stats on in advance, but I will speak to them briefly. But I'm very, very proud to say that, from a person's crimes perspective, we are 25% down from last year, and nearly 50% from four years ago. You guys still hear me? Yes, sir. Okay. Which is fantastic. From a property perspective, we're also at a four-year low, and a 32% drop compared to last year, as you'll see. And we're at lows in every area, except for theft-unders, we went up one offense from last year, but overall property crime is way, way down, which is fantastic. I'm very excited to see that. And then overall criminal code offenses, we're down 33%. So, I'm very excited to be able to present these stats, because to be honest, we haven't, in all my jurisdictions, I've never seen stats this low, and that's for 2020 compared to 2019 for the whole calendar year. In traffic enforcement slash motor vehicle accidents, you'll see there that we are basically exactly on par, nine accidents last year, and nine this year. But the very positive thing is, I think you guys are aware that we are a Vision Zero detachment, where our goal is to have zero fatal or injury collision. And we've achieved that goal for last year in Bruderheim. There was zero injury collisions, zero fatals. So, that's fantastic as well. I'm very proud of that. And that's it for the stats. I won't go any deeper, but you guys have had them and been able to review them. So, if you have any questions about specific offenses or anything, please feel free to ask them at the end. And then the other update I wanna have is that while you guys are very fortunate in your person's crimes are down considerably, including assaults, which are down 50% from last year, but not everywhere in our Forest of Saskatchewan Police and Jurisdiction has had the same luck over the last couple of years. So, I was fortunate enough to be able to create a domestic violence coordinator position. So, Corporal Jen Brown, you may know her. She's been around for a while, but she's actually has that expertise. So, she's taken on the position of domestic violence coordinator. Quite briefly, what she'll be doing is she'll provide expertise in reviewing every single domestic violence file that comes in our area so that she can be a extra set of eyes and a high level, again, expert view in terms of investigations, in terms of safety planning for the victim, and in terms of strategies. She's also able to partner with other agencies and where need be, jump in and investigate some of the more high risk or high profile domestic violence files. So, I'm very excited to have that position available now in our detachment. I will open the floor to questions. One thing I'll ask you guys to consider is we, starting in March, I'll be preparing the annual performance plan for next year. So, I can present whenever you would like. Sometime after April 1st, I can present last year's performance plan and how we did. But I'd like you, Council, and Your Worship to start either asking questions about next year's now, if you have them, while you have me in front of you, or at least thinking about if there's any specific priorities you want us to consider for next year as it's never too early to start planning. And that's all I have for you fine folks.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Great, thank you very much, Inspector Mike. Does anyone have any questions for Inspector Mike? Councilor Pat and then Councilor Judy.

speaker: patlee
text: Thanks for meeting with us tonight, Mike. I just wanna say kudos on the domestic violence coordinator you have in place. It's rough times right now for lots of families and to have something like this is, I feel quite proactive, timely, and once again, kudos. It says a lot.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Thank you.

speaker: judyschuelertow
text: Thank you.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Councilor Judy.

speaker: judyschuelertow
text: Yeah, thanks for coming out. Staff Sergeant Mike, or what's your official? Inspector Mike. Yes, Mike. Anyhow, thanks for coming out. A couple things. I noticed like our numbers went down. I kind of studied them there. I kind of attributed to the big COVID that's happening and everybody being locked down consistently. We can't do an awful lot. I'm surprised our domestic violence went down and I'm happy about it because you hear about those things happening and then when we see our numbers, I guess we're fortunate. So that's good. With COVID happening and stuff, are you planning or is there any plan to, as a government puts different things into place, are there any plans to hand out tickets or anything like that? People not abiding by the laws?

speaker: mikemccauley
text: So the philosophy of the government and by extension, the RCMP and myself is we are all about education first when it comes to COVID restriction and whatnot. However, by all means, we are armed with the ability to write a ticket should we need to. So for example, if people are, well, now you're allowed outdoor gatherings, but before when you weren't, if people were skating on a pond and they were skating together, we would go and the first thing we'd say is, hey guys, you got to keep separate. The only way it would turn into something worse is if they basically said, no, forget it, we're not going to. And then they continued that behavior. Well, that's when we would take an enforcement approach. Other example would be if there was a house party that we were called to and there was 40 people in a house, well, there's not much you can educate there because obviously people know better. So we might have to take, for example, possibly write the registered owner of the house to ticket or something like that. We will do those things, but our first goal is to do education first and hope that our citizens will do the right thing. Okay, good.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Thank you. Any other questions? Councilor George has a question.

speaker: georgecampbell
text: Has there been any calls to our area in regard to the COVID-19?

speaker: mikemccauley
text: Not that I am aware of, no. We've had very few calls to service, to be honest. There's a few more in Fort Saskatchewan proper with some of the outdoor facilities they have there, but no, to my knowledge, I can double check, but we definitely haven't written a ticket in Brunerheim. We may have had some verbal warnings, but few and far between.

speaker: georgecampbell
text: People are practicing good measures there.

speaker: mikemccauley
text: People are practicing good measures. I hope so, yeah. Either that or you guys don't want to call us.

speaker: georgecampbell
text: I noticed your presence is a little bit more in town. It's to do with traffic violations and the Traffic Act. We had a peace officer here last week. He even stopped me on my tractor. Just a reminder that I had to have a triangle on that.

speaker: mikemccauley
text: But he did his job. He did his job.

speaker: georgecampbell
text: Kudos to him.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Thank you, Councillor George. Deputy Mayor Dan.

speaker: Other
text: Thanks. Again, like everybody else said, Mike, thank you for taking the time to come out here and spend a little chit-chat with us. To build on what Judy was saying, how she said that it seems like maybe a lot of the numbers are a bit lower due to the pandemic and various other issues. You said that you guys are all staffed up now, so you're ready to go. Are you kind of thinking that this is a little bit of a calm before the storm? Should anybody be locking down, batting down the hatches and getting ready?

speaker: mikemccauley
text: Well, I almost lost a couple of my kids' sleds because of this current windstorm, but no, I mean, we can't predict it. I can tell you that Bruggerheim, there's no way to describe it except that when one of the small towns we police, Lamont and Shipman and yourselves, when it comes to the rural towns I find in my four years is that one town will spike because someone will move in that's a guy who likes to have sticky fingers and likes to steal. We'll notice those trends, we'll target them, and then a lot of times they'll move out of town. So Bruggerheim and Lamont have flipped this year. I remember two years ago, Bruggerheim was a bit higher and Lamont was a bit quieter, and now it seems like it's flipped. So I don't know if we've scared someone off to move into Lamont or whatever, but to have this big of a drop, absolutely COVID plays a little bit of a part, but I think it's showing that you guys are in really good shape, and hopefully there's no prolific criminals that are living in your area right now, which tends to spike the numbers.

speaker: Other
text: So we should just treat Lamont like Australia and just ship them all over there?

speaker: mikemccauley
text: I would never say that. For the record, in case I'm sure you guys all talk, I'm not saying Lamont's out of control or anything, it's just, but it seems like their numbers have remained somewhat constant, whereas yours have dropped considerably. So COVID, I would say COVID might have a 10%, just as an estimation, 10% drop in things overall, but to have drops like this, 50% and 32%, that's because I think we're doing our job in targeting people and patrolling so that people don't go and do crime there, hopefully.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Councillor Judy.

speaker: judyschuelertow
text: Yeah, and I will say, Mike, that I think you're patrolling out here and you're targeting has definitely helped. I've noticed myself or CMP around way more than they were the year before, and sometimes just the present makes people more aware of what's happening. And so thank you very much for that. I think that's got a lot to do with it.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Awesome, thanks. Anybody else, questions for Inspector Mike? A couple of things, Inspector Mike, I just want to say thanks again to your detachment and your leadership. Is my mic working okay? Yeah. Okay, and really appreciate this information. Are we able to share these stats on our website or anything with our citizens? Yeah, that's great. I just wanted to ask a question under the total federal, other provincial stats. It says a big jump there, and I'm not sure what that would be for. Which one, sir? Under total federal, it says other provincial stats. It says 16 in 2019 and 2020 is 41. Sorry, just trying to figure this out here. No worries. But it's encouraging to see the low statistics, and while you're looking for that- Is it on page one or page two? It's on this page. Page two, first. Page two, other federal, it says-

speaker: mikemccauley
text: Oh, for total provincial stats, Liquor Act, Cannabis Act, that one? Yeah, the one at the bottom there, other provincial stats, it says. Yes, sorry, I know, I see it. That encompasses like provincial tickets and whatnot, violation tickets, nearly. So you'll see Liquor Act, so that would be open liquor in a vehicle if they write a non-specific act. Cannabis Act, there's four, so that would be writing a violation ticket for cannabis in the vehicle, likely. And then other provincial stats, that could be a whole raft of different things. But that's our members writing tickets and writing offence enforcement things. So what I suggest is that that's a positive thing, because again, our presence is more known there. So I wouldn't worry too, too much about that. That's not crime, really. They're more just provincial statutes.

speaker: karlhauch
text: The other thing I was going to mention is with a smaller sample to draw from, when changes happen, you can really see some big changes in percentages. Sometimes we hear from residents that because of the crime in the past, they don't report things. And do you feel that that's a potential cause for some of this, or is that just a rant?

speaker: mikemccauley
text: It could be, I hope not. I mean, we've always encouraged, we've no call too small, like we want to hear from you guys. But I mean, absolutely, that could be, if your residents aren't calling us for a crime, then yeah, the numbers will drop. So, but I mean, theft of motor vehicle, nobody's not calling for a theft of motor vehicle, for example. And you see that that's gone down 64%. So, theft overs, most people like that. So if someone loses something over $5,000, they're going to call us, right? So I hope that's not the case, but it could be, it could be a part of it.

speaker: karlhauch
text: Very encouraging to hear that number 64% less on the vehicle thefts. Thank you very much. Testament to the good job you guys are doing for us. Thank you. Okay, thanks. Any other comments, questions for Inspector Mike? Councillor George.

speaker: georgecampbell
text: We were talking about the vehicle thefts. What do you attribute the downgrade of vehicle thefts to?

speaker: mikemccauley
text: Like I was saying, so what happens with vehicle thefts is typically if someone's stealing a car there, they're not going to drive all the way out to Bruderheim to steal a car. It would be someone, and this is just my opinion, with somebody local that would be stealing a car. So if you get a prolific offender that decides to rent space somewhere in Bruderheim, then their mode of transportation is to steal a car. So they might steal a car a week while they're living there. And often, if we see a trend like that, there's a spike we'll target. Like with our intelligence, we can often find out who's in town that might deserve more of our attention. So again, I would say, you know, there's a bit of luck to it and possibly a bit of our enforcement, you know, has deterred people from thinking Bruderheim's a quiet place where I can get away with things. You know, or maybe we put somebody in jail that used to steal a lot of cars there. There's a lot of those types of factors, but, and it could be a COVID related thing as well. The fact that people are at home now. So there's less of an opportunity to steal from them. That could be part of it as well. So you're saying maybe a car rustler moved on? Well, hopefully, yeah. Hopefully somewhere South or something. Lethbridge maybe.

speaker: karlhauch
text: And Micah, the final thing I wanted to add is a plug for our local help as Heartland Citizens on Patrol, working together with your detachment has been very good. Maybe that has some to do with it as well, but just thank you for your support of that organization.

speaker: mikemccauley
text: Yeah, absolutely. They're invaluable and volunteers like yourself are very much welcomed at our detachment. We really appreciate their work.
